### [Tables &amp; *p*-values](../tables/index.html)

<!-- BEN: de verwijzing naar de (Nederlandse) speelkist is weggelaten; het Engelse menu wijst
     alleen naar wat er in het Engels is. -->
A test statistic from a paper — *t*(38) = 2.24, *z* = 1.96 — and you see the *p*-value straight away, as an **area** under the curve, with the *z*, *t*, *F* and χ² tables beside it. A tool, not a toy.
:::

::: {.cc-card .cc-card-solomon}
### [The judgement of Solomon](../speeltjes/solomon-en.html)

<!-- MIEKE: "tot alleen de sensitisatie overblijft" — het vakwoord is eruit en vervangen door
     wat het betekent, in de woorden van solomon-en zelf ("what pretest and therapy do together").
     Rosie las "sensitisation" en "a regression all along" als de ontknoping van een film die ze
     niet had gezien. Alternatief: het vakwoord houden, "the sensitisation" (Brits) of
     "sensitization" (zoals solomon-en, Campbell & Stanley). -->
Four groups, one therapy, and a pretest that does something of its own. Step by step you take group I's improvement apart into four pieces, until only one is left: what the pretest and the therapy do together. And then you see that the whole thing was a regression all along.
:::

*De regressieve ruggengraat* — *The Regressive Backbone* — is a statistics textbook with the working notes left in: at the bottom of every page you can see where the author is still weighing things up, and where he still has his doubts. It is being written in Dutch, and you can read along as it grows. The first four chapters are on their way in English, with an R exercise book to go with them.
:::

## The doubt is left in

<!-- MIEKE: "wat het boek over onzekerheid beweert, doet het ook zelf" — gekozen "it practises
     what it preaches about uncertainty" (Rosie's eigen woorden voor wat ze las); alternatief
     "it does what it says about uncertainty" (dichter bij het Nederlands, zonder preek). -->
Statistics is the subject that takes uncertainty seriously. Oddly enough, statistics books rarely sound like it — they speak with the confidence of someone who has never had to think anything over. *The Regressive Backbone* keeps the two together: it practises what it preaches about uncertainty. Uncertainty is not a problem. It is contact with reality.

<!-- MIEKE: de knop heet in het (Nederlandse) boek "toon werknotities". Eerst stond dat label
     erbij; Rosie vroeg waarom haar een Nederlands woord werd verteld. Nu zonder label: "a button
     that opens the working notes". Of de Engelse hoofdstukken dezelfde knop krijgen, is nog niet
     besloten. "tweede leesniveau" — gekozen "a second way of reading"; alternatief "a second
     layer to read". -->
That is why every page of the book ends with a button that opens the working notes. There are two kinds. The first is the workbench — wordings still to be chosen between, a figure still to come. The second is the doubt, and that one is about you: *does the reader see here that this is about the population, or does it need to be sharper?* Under a question like that, the extra explanation is right there. If you're following, you simply read on; if you stall, you open the note and find exactly that piece. It is not a peek behind the scenes. It is a second way of reading.

<!-- MIEKE: "Blijf jij op zo'n plek even haken" — gekozen "get stuck there for a moment";
     alternatief "snag on a place like that". "Je staat naast de auteur in plaats van onder
     hem" — de "hem" is de auteur, zoals in het Nederlands. -->
And it does something else. Where the material is hard, the page now simply says so, in the words of someone who is still weighing up how to explain it. If you get stuck there for a moment, that is not down to you — that is where everyone's thinking stalls, the writer's included. You stand beside the author instead of beneath him. That's exactly where this book wants you to be.
